posts.title: Externalizing Hand Grip Pressure Through Real-Time Visual Feedback
From young aces to injury cases: a qualitative study of stakeholder perspectives on injury risk in junior to elite badminton
posts.summary: Researchers looked at how experts judge injury risk when young badminton players move to elite level. Twenty national-level stakeholders including coaches, athletes, doctors and physios were interviewed. Experts relied on experience-based cues like pressure, recovery and attitude rather than objective factors.

posts.title: Epidemiology of injuries in elite male volleyball players over a full season: A retrospective study
posts.venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
posts.summary: Researchers tracked time-loss injuries over a full season in elite male volleyball players in Taiwan’s Top Volleyball League using a self-administered questionnaire. About a third of players reported a time-loss injury, with an overall rate of 4.3 per 1000 athlete exposures. Outside hitters had a higher injury rate than liberos, while age and body mass index showed no significant association.

posts.title: Predicting Performance in Badminton based on BDNF Val66Met Gene Polymorphism among Badminton Players
posts.venue: International Journal of Racket Sports Science
posts.summary: The study examined whether the BDNF Val66Met gene variant relates to performance and injury history in badminton. Buccal swabs and physical tests were done on 101 highly trained men who play badminton. The variant was linked to reaction speed, with a correlation of r = 0.230 for simple reaction time and ValVal carriers showing faster simple and choice reaction times than MetMet carriers.

posts.title: A Comparison of Mean and Peak Internal Training and Competition Physical Demands in Professional Male Basketball Players
posts.summary: Researchers looked at average and peak heart rate, oxygen consumption and respiratory rate in pro male basketball players. Measurements were taken during five pre-season matches and twenty training sessions in Spain’s top league. Peak measures rose more in competition than in practice, but average measures were largely alike.
posts.forWhom: basketball players interested in training versus game demands

posts.title: Physical Activity During Official Match Play in Female Masters Basketball Players: An Accelerometry-Based Study
posts.summary: Researchers used tri-axial microsensors to measure activity intensity and external load during official matches at a three-day national masters tournament. Fifty-two female masters basketball players aged 37 to 63 took part. Time in activity zones differed, with light and vigorous activity higher than moderate, and moderate-to-vigorous activity summed to about 42.78 minutes per match.
posts.forWhom: Female masters players and members over forty

posts.title: Comparison of Physical Activity and Stress Levels of Individuals Playing Pickleball in Türkiye and Abroad
posts.summary: Researchers compared physical activity and perceived stress in pickleball players in Türkiye and abroad using scales and statistical analysis. 144 players took part. Physical activity scores did not differ significantly between the Turkish and foreign groups, but perceived stress scores did differ significantly.
posts.forWhom: pickleball regulars interested in stress and activity

posts.title: Externalizing Hand Grip Pressure Through Real-Time Visual Feedback
posts.summary: Researchers tested how different real-time visual displays of hand grip pressure help novices match pressure. 28 novices did baseball and table tennis grip tasks with an instrumented glove. A continuous gradient display led to more accurate pressure matching and more focused gaze than a discrete bar display, even though people thought the bar was more precise.
posts.forWhom: tennis players curious about grip feel
